subject.title: memory flush never triggers when reserveTokensFloor equals contextWindow

question: For oversized `reserveTokensFloor` values in memory flush and preflight compaction, should OpenClaw clamp the effective runtime threshold, reject or warn on the config, or migrate/document a different policy?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but changing an existing compaction reserve setting can affect upgrade behavior, prompt budget, and memory persistence timing for real users.

options.title: Central effective clamp
options.body: Clamp the effective reserve or threshold in the shared memory-flush/preflight gate, preserve the config value, warn when useful, and add focused regression tests.

options.title: Config validation and doctor path
options.body: Treat oversized reserve floors as invalid configuration and add explicit doctor/docs handling before changing runtime behavior.

options.title: Defer to adjacent budget PRs
options.body: Hold this issue until maintainers decide whether the broader reserve-token and soft-threshold PRs should own the policy instead.

recommendation.title: Central effective clamp
recommendation.body: Clamp the effective reserve or threshold in the shared memory-flush/preflight gate, preserve the config value, warn when useful, and add focused regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The original memory-flush implementation and current policy decision are closest to this area history.
